title: Renewal Timing and Company-Initiated Termination References for the Named Non-Owner Policy
content:
Renewal timing on the Named Non-Owner Policy is set by package; the references for company-initiated terminations are common to all packages.

| Package | Renewal term issued this many calendar days before expiration | Late-renewal window after expiration (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner Minimum Limits | 30 | 0 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner Minimum Limits with UM | 30 | 0 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner 50/100/50 | 30 | 0 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner 100/200/50 | 30 | 5 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner 100/300/50 | 45 | 5 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner 250/500/100 | 45 | 10 |

The late-renewal window is the number of calendar days after expiration during which the renewal down payment is still accepted, renewing with a lapse. A window of 0 days leaves no day after the expiration date on which the renewal can still be accepted.

**References common to every package**

- Minimum nonrenewal notice days: the Owner Auto Policy's nonrenewal notice days by state (single source).
- New-business underwriting periods: the Owner Auto Policy's new-business underwriting period days by state (single source).
- Advance notice days for underwriting cancellations: the Owner Auto Policy's underwriting cancellation notice days by state (single source).
- Underwriting reasons for which an in-force term may be cancelled after the underwriting period: the named insured acquired a vehicle or regular use of one; material misrepresentation on the application.

**Hypothetical timing.** A Cardinal Point Non-Owner 250/500/100 term expiring on 20 August has its renewal term issued on 6 July (45 days before), and a renewal down payment is still accepted through 30 August (expiration day 0 plus 10 days). On Cardinal Point Non-Owner 50/100/50 the renewal must be accepted no later than the expiration date itself.
